sentences.text:
This is a curious case, where the victim who was alleged to have been raped by respondent accused no.1 got pregnant, had approached the respondent accused no.2 who was a mid-wife seeking abortion, and during the course of such NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/123/1998 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2025 undefined attempt of abortion, she suffered grievous internal injuries for which, she sought treatment and after having recovered, was discharged from the hospital and thereafter, had passed away after a period of 6 months.
2.

The Special Case against both the respondents- accused was conducted before the learned Special Judge and Additional Sessions Judge of Jamnagar, who was pleased to acquit both the respondents-accused of the charges framed against them under Sections 376, 506(2), 304-A, 312,
314 and 338 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3(1)(11) of the Prevention of Atrocities Act.

3. The complainant-State being aggrieved by the said judgment and order of acquittal of the learned Special Judge and Additional Sessions NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/123/1998 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2025 undefined Judge of Jamnagar pronounced on 05.09.1997 in Special Case No.59 of 1994, had preferred the present appeal challenging the said acquittal.

sentences.text: 4. As per the prosecution case, in the year of 1994 during the Diwali festivals, the victim had gone to collect money from the respondent-accused no.1.
However, instead of paying her the money, he had committed rape upon her and had threatened her with her life.
Thereafter, the victim had approached the respondent-accused no.2 on 10.01.1994 since, her menstrual cycles had stopped and she had feared that she was pregnant.

The respondent accused no.2 who was an untrained midwife,
had conducted surgery which had resulted into the victim's health having deteriorated, and as such,
she was admitted to Ankur Hospital and Maternity Home at Jamnagar, from where, she was referred to NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/123/1998 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2025
undefined
Irwin Hospital, where, the doctors had conducted surgeries and the victim upon having recovered and being fit, was discharged from the said hospital on 31.01.1994.

However, thereafter, she had passed away on 11.06.1994.
5.

The FIR came to be lodged by the victim herself on 17.01.1994 which was produced on record vide exhibit-18, wherein, she had narrated the incident which had occurred during the period of Diwali festival.

She had narrated as to how she had gone to the respondent accused no.1's house to collect the amount of Rs.600/- and instead of repaying the said amount, the respondent accused no.1 had committed rape upon her.
She had also mentioned in her FIR that, since it was festival time, she had not disclosed about the incident to anyone.

However, thereafter, she had disclosed about the said incident to her parents, NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/123/1998 JUDGMENT DATED:
08/10/2025 undefined but, they had not deemed it fit to lodge a police complaint, lest their reputation would get tarnished.
She had also mentioned in the FIR about how the respondent accused no.2 had severed her intestine and had caused grievous internal injuries.

6. The victim while being admitted in the Irwin hospital, the Executive Magistrate had recorded her dying declaration, wherein also, she had narrated about the incident and the roles of both the State Of Gujarat vs Raja Mahmed Saiyed Alias Raju Madrasi on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55113994/
2 respondents-accused.
7.

sentences.text: The Investigating Officer had recorded the statements of the relevant witnesses and there being enough culpable evidence against the respondents-accused, had filed the charge sheet before the concerned Court.

8. The learned Special Judge and Additional NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/123/1998 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2025 undefined Sessions Judge of Jamnagar had framed the charge against the respondents-accused, to which, they having denied were put to trial.
The prosecution, to bring home the guilt of the respondents-accused, had examined 12 witnesses and had produced 30 documents in support of such oral evidence.

9. Upon completion of oral evidence and after recording the statements of the respondents- accused under section 313 of the CRPC, and after hearing the learned advocates of either side, the learned Special Judge and Additional Sessions Judge of Jamnagar, was pleased to acquit the respondents-accused of the charges, which were framed against them.

10. The learned APP Ms.Vrunda Shah on behalf of the complainant-State has taken us through the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/123/1998 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2025 undefined entire record and proceedings of Special Case No.59 of 1994 and has also submitted a gist of the relevant evidence which was produced before the learned Trial Court.
11. None is present on behalf of the respondent- accused.

12. At the outset, on perusing the record and proceedings of the Special Case No.59 of 1994, the following aspects have emerged:
(a) Neither the victim nor her parents had lodged the complaint against the respondents- accused immediately after the incident, which had occurred during the Diwali festival.
(b) The victim though being subjected to rape, not having disclosed about the said fact to either her parents or any of her family members NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/123/1998 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2025 undefined during the initial period.
(c) Though the Investigating Officer had collected the Muddamal and there was serology report to that effect at Exhibit-34, the said discovery panchnama is neither proved through the deposition of PW-3 Gani Mohammad who was the panch witness, nor PW-7 the Investigating Officer.
(d) Upon sifting through the entire evidence, it overtly appears

that the victim had not mentioned about the respondent-accused no.1 having committed rape upon her and respondent-accused no.2 State Of Gujarat vs Raja Mahmed Saiyed Alias Raju Madrasi on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55113994/
3 having caused her grievous injuries while aborting her foetus.

sentences.text: (e) The prosecution had examined PW-5 Pamiben Bhimjibhai vide Exh.15 and PW-6 NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/123/1998 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2025 undefined Bhima Harji vide Exh.16, who were the parents of the victim.
Both of them had not supported the prosecution case and were declared hostile.

Rather, both of them in their respective cross- examinations conducted by the learned advocate for the accused had stated that, neither they nor their daughter i.e. the victim, had filed any complaint against the respondents-accused.

Also, both of them had stated that,
their daughter had returned home after having been discharged from the hospital on 31.01.1994.

(f) The victim being discharged from the hospital on 31.01.1994 after having recovered, had died after almost 5 to 6 months and there were neither medical case papers nor allegations as regards deterioration of her health because of the injuries, which were NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/123/1998 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2025 undefined caused by the respondent-accused no.2, during the intervening period.
(g) The postmortem of the victim was not done who ultimately passed away on 11.06.1994.

(h) Though as per the FIR and the dying declaration before the Executive Magistrate, the victim has stated that she had continuously raised alarms while she was subjected to rape, the Investigating Officer - PW-7, Maheshkumar Rameshwar Gupta in his deposition at Exh-17 had admitted in his cross-examination that "it was true that during his investigation, it was not revealed from the neighbours of respondent accused no.1 that they had heard alarms."
Thus, except this fact, there is no iota of evidence about the respondent accused no.1 having committed rape upon the victim.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/123/1998 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2025 undefined
(i) It also transpires that, the victim had gone to Irwin hospital after one and a half months of the incident, for abortion.
However, as per the deposition of PW-2, Naveenchandra Kanjibhai Haria, the foetus was around 12 to 15 weeks.

(j) PW-1 Dr.Ashok Kumar Ghanshyambhai Bhatt who was examined vide Exhibit-10, in his deposition had submitted that, though the victim had come to his Ankur Hospital and Maternity Home on 10.01.1994, he was unable to produce any case papers as regards her examination.
It was this witness who had stated about the presence of respondent accused no.2 along with the victim before him.
However, he had only stated that, the respondent accused no.2 had accompanied the victim and nothing more.

Rather, he had stated that, the victim had not uttered the name of the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/123/1998 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2025 undefined respondent-accused no.2 and had only informed him that, she had approached a woman for her abortion, who had refused to do so.

(k) The prosecution had examined PW-11 Dr. Yaminiben Jitendrabhai Vasavada vide Exh-44 and Dr.Demilaben Shantilal Shah vide Exh-45 who were attached with the Gynecology Department of Irwin hospital at the relevant time.

Except the internal injuries which were sustained by the victim,

(l) The medical case papers which were submitted on record did not disclose about the roles of the respondent accused no.1 and NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/123/1998 JUDGMENT DATED:

(m)The medico legal certificate which was given by the Irvin Hospital which was produced on record at Exh.46, stated about the victim having been admitted to Irvin Hospital on 10.01.1994 with history of two and half months of amenorrhea with profuse bleeding per vaginum since 6 hours following interference outside by untrained dai.
She was examined by me and she was found pregnant with 10-12 weeks of pregnancy with bleeding peruganum.
Findings were confirmed by Dr.Yamini Vasavada.

(n) The said certificate neither mentioned about rape having been committed with the victim, nor the name of the respondent accused no.1 as the rapist nor the name of the respondent- accused no.2 being the untrained Dai.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/123/1998 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2025 undefined (o) There being no evidence about the death of the victim having resulted from rape and subsequent abortion.
13.
The learned competent Court had noted all the above aspects in its judgement and had given sound reasonings to disbelieve the prosecution case.
Hence, we would not like to delve upon and reiterate the same.

14. Upon considering the entire evidence, it would not be out of context to take note of the fact that,
the Investigating Officer could have sincerely and seriously investigated considering the allegations about heinous offense having been committed with the victim, which ultimately resulted in her death. However, the entire investigation not only appeared to be devoid of bona-fides, but also, was botched up.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/123/1998 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2025 undefined 15.
The prosecution had grossly failed to prove the charges against the respondents-accused which ultimately resulted in their acquittal.
16. At this juncture, we may refer to some of the propositions enunciated by the Supreme Court with regard to exercise of appellate jurisdiction in acquittal appeals.

In case of Sanjeev v. State of Himachal Pradesh reported in 2022 (6) SCC 294, para 7 reads as under:
"7.

State of Karnataka3, Anwar Ali and another v. State of Himachal Pradesh).
7.2

7.3 If two views are possible from the evidence on record, the appellate Court must NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/123/1998 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2025 undefined be extremely slow in interfering with the appeal against acquittal (See Sambasivan and others v. State of Kerala)."
17.

"6.

322

sentences.text: It is true that while deciding an appeal against acquittal, the Appellate Court has to reappreciate the evidence.

After re- appreciating the evidence, the first question that needs to be answered by the Appellate Court is whether the view taken by the Trial Court was a plausible view that could have been taken based on evidence on record.
Perusal of the impugned judgment of the High Court shows that this question has not been adverted to.

Appellate Court can interfere with the order of acquittal only if it is satisfied after reappreciating the evidence that the only possible conclusion was that the guilt of the accused had been established beyond a reasonable doubt.
The Appellate Court cannot overturn order of acquittal only on the ground that another view is possible.
In other words, the judgment of acquittal must be found to be perverse.
Unless the Appellate Court records such a finding, no interference can be made with the order of acquittal.
The High Court has ignored the well-settled principle that an order of acquittal further strengthens the presumption of innocence of the 326 [2024] 4 S.C.R. Digital Supreme Court Reports accused.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/123/1998 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2025 undefined
After having perused the judgment, we find that the High Court has not addressed itself on the main question."

18. It is also a settled legal position that in acquittal appeals, the appellate court is not required to re- write the judgement or to give fresh reasonings, when the reasons assigned by the Court below are found to be just and proper.

Such principle is laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of Karnataka Vs. Hemareddy, reported in AIR 1981 SC 1417 wherein it is held as under:
"... This court has observed in Girija Nandini Devi V. Bigendra Nandini Chaudhary (1967)1 SCR 93: (AIR 1967 SC 1124) that it is not the duty of the appellate court when it agrees with the view of the trial court on the evidence to repeat the narration of the State Of Gujarat vs Raja Mahmed Saiyed Alias Raju Madrasi on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55113994/
6 evidence or to reiterate the reasons given by the trial court expression of general agreement with the reasons given by the Court the decision of which is under appeal,
will ordinarily suffice."

Thus, in case the appellate court agrees with NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/123/1998 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2025 undefined the reasons and the opinion given by the competent court below,
then the discussion of evidence at length is not necessary.
19. We have re-appreciated and re-evaluated the evidence rendered in Special Case No.59 of 1994 on the touchstone of latest decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court.

Considering the evidence in its entirety, we are of the considered opinion that the learned Special Judge and Sessions Judge has rightly, correctly and legally appreciated the evidence which was rendered before him, pursuant to which, he had acquitted the respondents-accused from the charges framed against them.
Thus, the judgement rendered in Special Case No.59 of 1994 does not require any interference and the same is upheld accordingly.
20. Consequently, the appeal is hereby dismissed.
